input.description: Find which activities host the drawer
Check home and Connect drawer click handling

content.text:
I'd keep `currentDrawerSection` on the activity, and have the activity pass it to the drawer rather than having the adapter work it out.

**Why the adapter can't find it on its own**

- Each activity that shows the drawer builds its own `BaseDrawerController`, which creates a new `NavDrawerAdapter`. Nothing in the adapter survives from one activity to the next.
- The only thing the adapter could remember is the last item tapped. That's often not the screen you're on:
  - Back navigation takes you to an earlier screen while the last tap still points at the later one.
  - Notifications open `ConnectMessagingActivity` directly, with no tap in the drawer.
  - The activity can be recreated after a configuration change or the process being killed.
  - `LoginActivity` and `CommCareSetupActivity` show the drawer without being any section.
- Which section you're in is a fixed fact about the screen. A one-line override in `PersonalIdWorkHistoryActivity` and `ConnectMessagingActivity` is the simplest reliable place to state it.

**Alternatives, and why I don't recommend them**

- **A `when (this) { is ConnectMessagingActivity -> MESSAGING … }` check in `BaseDrawerActivity`:** this puts it all in one place, but the base class then has to know about its subclasses. Every new section screen means editing the base class.
- **An intent extra set when the drawer launches a screen:** this breaks for any screen opened another way, such as from a notification or a deep link.

**What would actually improve things**

Pass the section into `BaseDrawerController` as a constructor argument, next to `onItemClicked`:
- The controller could then handle the "tapped the section I'm already in → just close the drawer" case itself. That would take it out of `BaseDrawerActivity.handleDrawerItemClick`.
- The adapter could also highlight the current item, which is the one real reason for the adapter to know about it.

The section would still come from the activity, but the drawer would own what happens because of it.

**Two things I noticed while checking this**

- `StandardHomeActivity` shows the drawer but doesn't set a section, so `currentDrawerSection` is `null` there. It overrides `handleDrawerItemClick` (`StandardHomeActivity.java:246`), which probably covers it, but I haven't read that override. As written, the comment in `BaseDrawerActivity.kt:83` is wrong about it: it says only Login and Setup reach that branch without a section, and the home screen also has none.
- `ConnectActivity` (Opportunities) is a drawer host through `NavigationHostCommCareActivity`, but it doesn't set `OPPORTUNITIES` as its section. That matters if Opportunities is meant to be a section like Messaging and Work History.

If you want, I can move the section into the controller.

input.description: Find setContentView calls in drawer activities

content.text:
`Activity.onContentChanged()` is a callback the window makes whenever the activity's content view changes. In practice it runs:

- **Inside every `setContentView(...)` call** (layout id, `View`, or `View` with params) and every `addContentView(...)` call. With `AppCompatActivity`, the delegate calls it right after it inflates your layout into the content frame.
- **Before `setContentView` returns.** So in `onCreate` it runs before any line after your `setContentView`.

It doesn't run when you change views inside the content, add or replace fragments, or navigate between Navigation destinations. It also doesn't run again on `onResume`.

What this means for `BaseDrawerActivity`:

1. **The drawer is set up in the middle of `onCreate`.** In this codebase the content view is set in three places:
   - `NavigationHostCommCareActivity.kt:16`
   - `PersonalIdWorkHistoryActivity.kt:35`
   - `ManagedUiFramework.setContentView` in `CommCareActivity.java:193`, for `@ManagedUi` activities such as Login and Setup

   `shouldShowDrawer()` and `setupDrawerController()` run at that moment. Any subclass field set after `setContentView` in `onCreate` isn't ready yet. That's likely why `ConnectMessagingActivity` connects `setDrawerTopLevel` in `onPostCreate` (after `navController` exists) rather than earlier.

2. **Every `setContentView` call builds a new drawer.** Each call creates another `BaseDrawerController` and calls `setupDrawer()` again. That adds another `DrawerListener` and registers `NotificationBroadcastHelper` again. Right now each activity appears to set its content view once, so this only becomes a problem if an activity starts calling it again (for example to swap layouts) or ends up calling it twice.

The drawer's views only exist after the layout is inflated, and the base class can't control when a subclass calls `setContentView`. That's why the setup is in this callback. If the drawer ever needs to wait until `onCreate` has finished, `onPostCreate` is the usual place.
